text:
mike: Quick heads-up — observed token attribution drift for requests with no X-API-Version header. Console shows a lot of v2 traffic but billing is attributing spikes to v1. anyone else seeing this?

anya: yep, noticed it last night around 03:10 UTC. tenant-42 had unexpected v1 quota consumption. logs show a bunch of requests missing the header and then being routed by the default router.

ravi: short diagnosis — when header missing we let the router pick a variant; some legacy proxies still tag the route key as "api_v1" before the billing join. billing reads route_key and uses that for attribution.

peggy: we should surface whether a request was "client-declared" vs "server-attributed" in telemetry. otherwise Console / billing will always disagree.

samir: concrete suggestion: add a small enum field to access logs and usage records: "version_attribution": "client|server|inferred". start by sampling ambiguous (header-missing) requests at 5%, capture full context.

mike: 5% seems reasonable. full-100% would be costly on heavy tenants. for error cases (mismatch in attribution vs declared) maybe 100% capture for 1h to debug.

anya: Console UX ask: expose a toggle "Group metrics by declared version / attributed version" and show a yellow banner when mismatch ratio > 1% for a tenant. makes it obvious to customers.

ravi: implementation notes: logging hook in router should set version_attribution and either copy declared header or inferred value. we can append to existing access log proto to avoid schema churn: new optional string. usage kafka topic will carry it; billing join needs a small schema tweak to prefer attributed when available.

peggy: runbook for oncall: if customer reports unexplained v1 billing, check "mismatch_ratio" metric; if >1% open a tracing capture job for that tenant and enable 100% capture for 30m.

samir: quick PoC in router:
```js
// pseudocode
if (!req.headers['x-api-version']) {
  req.headers['x-version-inferred'] = inferVersion(req); // inspects model_name, seqlen, prompt hints
  meta.version_attribution = 'inferred';
} else {
  meta.version_attribution = 'client';
}
emitAccessLog(req, meta);
```
Works without breaking old proxies.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: router-infer-version -> canary us-west-1 at 10:15 UTC (10% traffic).

kpi-bot: sampling plan summary: start 5% ambiguous sampling global, canary router-infer-version at 10% traffic, escalate sampling to 20% if tenant-level mismatch > 0.5% sustained for 6h.

mike: decision checklist (agreed):
- add version_attribution to access logs (ravi owner)
- start 5% ambiguous sampling, 100% on error windows (samir owner for sampling)
- Console toggle to view by declared/attributed + banner for >1% mismatch (peggy owner)
- billing join to prefer attributed when present; keep declared in audit (anya owner)
- canary deploy for router change tomorrow (deploy-bot scheduled)

anya: noted. I'll open the billing GH issue and link the runbook steps.

ravi: one more subtlety — rate limits and quota enforcement. we should enforce against the attributed version (server-determined) to avoid a client spoofing declared header and bypassing limits. but keep declared value in audit logs for forensic.

peggy: agree. enforcement = attributed, visibility = both. Console will show both fields in request inspector.

mike: great. please add short retro item: check whether any backfilled attribution changes require billing adjustments (we might need a grace/credit path).

samir: will do a backfill script prototype for a 7-day window, using model_name heuristics when attribution missing; will surface confidence score so billing can decide.

mike: thanks team. I'll post follow-up with GH links + canary timeline.

peggy: also adding a tiny UX note — when showing split charts we should default to "attributed" for internal usage views and "declared" for raw traffic view. keeps customer-facing defaults less surprising. :+1:

mike: perfect. closing this thread, will update when GH PRs are live.
